clue.text: A most unusual church organ

indicators.note: unusual tells us the letters of 'A most' are set out in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Someone marvels at a church organ that is quite out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organ' looks like the church instrument, and 'most unusual' like one phrase, but the organ is a body part and 'most' belongs to the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The stomach is an internal body part with a function, which is what an organ is in anatomy.

clue.text: Finished lower than second as idle

indicators.note: lower than places the finished word below the second in this down entry

parts.note: a tick is a moment, a second
over means finished

explanation.surface: A racing result: someone finished behind second place, as an also-ran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'idle' here is the verb, of an engine running slowly with no load.
explanation.definitionFit: An engine that ticks over is running slowly while out of gear, which is what idling means.

clue.text: Delivery post procedure subject to doctor

indicators.note: subject to puts the procedure under the doctor in this down entry

parts.note: post and mail are synonyms
an op is a surgical procedure, an operation

explanation.surface: A post-operative routine supervised by a medic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post procedure' reads as after an operation, but post is the letters sent and the procedure is the op.
explanation.definitionFit: A mail drop is a drop-off of letters, a single delivery of post to an address or box.

clue.text: Person in suit taps vacantly and stews

indicators.note: in places the person inside the legal case

parts.note: a suit is a legal case
a soul is a person

indicators.note: vacantly means emptied of the inside letters, leaving only the outer two

parts.note: the first and last letters of taps

explanation.surface: A man in a business suit taps away absently while fretting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit, a CASE, not clothing; 'stews' looks like a verb for worrying but is the plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassoulets are slow-cooked French dishes of beans and meat, a kind of stew.

clue.text: Clean coat put on by artist

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a thin layer of diluted paint or ink applied by a painter

explanation.walkthrough: The surface pictures a painter cleaning a coat, but the second stretch is a thin wash of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Wash is a verb for cleaning with water, and a noun for a thin translucent layer of watercolour.

clue.text: Power in drubbings lifted state of shock

indicators.note: lifted means read upwards in this down entry, so the letters are turned round
in puts the power letter inside the word for drubbings

parts.note: routs are heavy defeats, drubbings
P is the symbol for power

explanation.surface: A team lifted by power in a series of thrashings is left dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: P goes inside ROUTS to make ROPUTS, then 'lifted' turns it upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A stupor is a dazed condition of near-unconsciousness, as after a shock.

clue.text: Creature found in vehicle I purchased with 50 per cent off

parts.note: a car is a vehicle

indicators.note: with 50 per cent off means only the front half of the purchase word is kept

parts.note: bought means purchased

explanation.surface: An animal spotted in a car someone bought at half price.
explanation.walkthrough: BOUGHT has six letters, so half off leaves BOU.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou is the North American reindeer, a large wild deer and so a creature.

clue.text: Put off seeing inspector's enthusiasm cut short

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector, so DI'S is inspector's

indicators.note: cut short means the enthusiasm word loses its last letter

parts.note: gusto is zest, enthusiasm

explanation.surface: Someone is deterred on seeing a police inspector's eagerness curbed.
explanation.walkthrough: DI stands for Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: To disgust someone is to repel them, causing revulsion that puts them off.

clue.text: Processed meat gone with butter by one

parts.note: past means gone, over and done with
a ram is something that butts
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A description of a sandwich: stale cured meat served alongside butter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'butter' is not the dairy spread but one who butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is a cured, smoked and spiced beef, a classic deli cold cut.

clue.text: Block out bits of film seen during middle of week

indicators.note: seen during places the film bits within the other letters
middle of picks out the central pair of letters of the four-letter word week

parts.note: the two central letters of week
clips are short extracts of film

explanation.surface: A film editor cuts out some footage in midweek.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle of a four-letter word is its central two letters, not a single one.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to obscure or cut off the light of something, as the moon does the sun.

clue.text: Great wife with a desire to keep quiet

parts.note: W is the abbreviation for wife in genealogies

indicators.note: to keep means the longer word holds the quiet letter inside it

parts.note: hoping means wanting, with a desire
P is piano, the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: A wife hopes to keep things hushed, and it is a big wish.
explanation.definitionFit: Whopping is an informal word for huge, so it matches great in the sense of very large.

clue.text: Plant with due respect to designated area in office

parts.note: a plant is a factory, the works
pace, from Latin, is used to mean with due respect to someone you disagree with

explanation.surface: A formal-sounding memo about a factory and an allotted office zone.
explanation.walkthrough: PACE (two syllables) is the Latin-derived 'with due respect to', used politely before naming someone one disagrees with.
explanation.definitionFit: A workspace is the area set aside for one person to work, such as a desk zone in an office.

clue.text: Bad luck, seeing which people perform for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means the words are to be heard, as by listeners in a theatre

parts.note: who do: which people perform, read as a question about the performers

explanation.surface: A superstitious actor reflects on which performers bring misfortune to a show.
explanation.walkthrough: Said aloud, WHO DO matches the answer; theatre talk of performers and audience disguises the sound signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A hoodoo is a jinx, something or someone thought to bring misfortune.

clue.text: A scream from university sportsman — several heading off

parts.note: a pro is a professional sportsman

indicators.note: heading off means the first letter of the word for several is removed

parts.note: various means several

explanation.surface: A rowing student lets out a yell as several teammates leave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A scream' sounds like a noise, but it is the informal sense of something hilarious; 'several heading off' takes the V off VARIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a scream means it is hilariously funny, which is what uproarious means in 'it was uproarious'.

clue.text: Prepared to act — that must change before day breaks

indicators.note: must change says the letters of that are rearranged

parts.note: ere is a poetic word for before

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of day are broken up and reassembled

explanation.surface: An urgent call to change things before daybreak.
explanation.walkthrough: THAT rearranged gives ATTH, then ERE, then DAY rearranged gives ADY. 'day breaks' looks like dawn.
explanation.definitionFit: At the ready means poised and ready for immediate use or action.

clue.text: Sauce requiring no time or money

indicators.note: requiring no means the sauce is made without the time letter

parts.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce

explanation.surface: A cheap, quick sauce that costs neither time nor money.
explanation.definitionFit: The peso is the currency unit of Mexico and several other Latin American countries.

clue.text: This could close media enquiry without conclusion

parts.note: the press means the news media

indicators.note: without conclusion means the last letter of the enquiry word is dropped

parts.note: a study is an investigation or enquiry

explanation.surface: A press investigation that never reaches its end could be shut down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like ending the enquiry, but it means fasten: the answer is a fastener.
explanation.definitionFit: A press stud is a snap fastener used to do up clothing, so it is something that closes.

clue.text: Bread ultimately fed poorest vagrant

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word fed
vagrant means wandering, so the letters of poorest wander into a new order

explanation.surface: A charity scene: bread finally given to the poorest homeless person.
explanation.walkthrough: Doorstep is British slang for a thick slice of bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A doorstep is a very thick slice of bread, named for its chunky size.

clue.text: Weapon fired up in dispute

indicators.note: in puts the turned word inside the dispute

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or argument

indicators.note: up means read upwards in this down entry, so the letters are turned round

parts.note: lit means set on fire

explanation.surface: Someone, fired up during an argument, draws a weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired up' reads as one phrase meaning angry, but the two words split: one gives a synonym and the other turns it, in a down entry. A set-to is a quarrel.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a short dagger with a slender tapering blade.

clue.text: Promoted spooks will take 30 days to get clean

indicators.note: will take means the spies hold the month inside them
promoted means moved up, so in this down entry the letters read upwards

parts.note: the CIA is the US intelligence agency, home to spooks
September has thirty days; SEPT is its abbreviation

explanation.surface: Promoted spies are given a month to clean up their act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Thirty days hath September' is the rhyme behind SEPT; CIA upward gives AIC to hold it.
explanation.definitionFit: Aseptic means free from bacteria or contamination, so sterile and clean.

clue.text: Loans due after roughly the beginning of the month

indicators.note: after places the loan word following the word for roughly

parts.note: ca, short for circa, means roughly
lends means loans, as a verb

explanation.surface: A borrower's reminder that repayments fall due around the first of the month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Loans' looks like a noun but is the verb, giving LENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Roman calendar the calends was the first day of each month.

clue.text: Pledge unbounded hate

indicators.note: unbounded means the word has lost its boundaries, its first and last letters

parts.note: loathe means hate

explanation.surface: A vow of limitless hatred.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unbounded' looks like a description of the hatred, but it strips LOATHE of its outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An oath is a solemn promise or vow, so it is a pledge.

clue.text: Underwear with lace designed for model

parts.note: smalls is British slang for underwear

indicators.note: designed suggests the letters of lace are fashioned into a new pattern

explanation.surface: A lingerie fashion description: underwear with designer lace for a catwalk model.
explanation.walkthrough: Smalls is British slang for underwear. 'model' looks like the catwalk sort, but it means a miniature replica.
explanation.definitionFit: A model is a reduced copy of something, and small-scale describes exactly that kind of reduced replica.

clue.text: Endure Lombardy on vacation, bringing up the rear

parts.note: to last is to endure

indicators.note: on vacation means emptied out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Lombardy

explanation.surface: A traveller puts up with an Italian holiday in Lombardy, trailing at the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on vacation' looks like a trip, but vacating Lombardy empties it to its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: Lastly means finally, in the last position, at the end of a sequence.

clue.text: Bank on resistance accepting answer, but not often

indicators.note: accepting means the answer letter is taken inside the other letters

parts.note: R is the symbol for electrical resistance
to bank on is to rely on

explanation.surface: A cautious person seldom counts on resistance, even when the answer is accepted.
explanation.definitionFit: Rarely means seldom, happening only on infrequent occasions.

clue.text: Satisfaction guaranteed following appeal

indicators.note: following puts the word for guaranteed after the appeal

parts.note: a plea is an appeal or request
sure means certain, guaranteed

explanation.surface: An advertising line promising satisfaction after a customer complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Pleasure is a feeling of enjoyment or contentment, close to satisfaction.

clue.text: Farrow can but produce one!

parts.note: a farrow is a litter of piglets; a sow can only produce one smallest, weakest piglet per litter

explanation.walkthrough: Farrow looks like a surname, but it is a litter of pigs; the joke is that only one piglet can be the smallest.
explanation.definitionFit: The runt is the smallest and weakest animal in a litter.

clue.text: Couldn't a thankyou be a work of music?

parts.note: can't means cannot, the present form standing in for couldn't
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a musical piece could take the form of a thank-you.
explanation.walkthrough: Ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantata is a composition for voices and instruments, often religious, so it is a musical piece.

clue.text: Lazy and cheeky son to be replaced by daughter

indicators.note: to be replaced by means the son letter gives way to the daughter letter

parts.note: insolent means rude, cheeky

explanation.surface: A family moan: the idle, rude son is swapped for a daughter.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means idle, disinclined to make any effort.

clue.text: Indication of second unknown politician backing test

parts.note: Y is an algebraic unknown
an MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: backing means the test word is turned to face the other way

parts.note: the MOT is the annual roadworthiness test for British vehicles

explanation.surface: A sign that a minor politician is supporting some trial.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is Britain's compulsory annual roadworthiness check for vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A symptom is a sign or signal of an underlying condition, such as a disease.
